output.title: What transcript accuracy hides in a small business workflow
output.body:
Transcript accuracy can hide the part that actually changes the decision: tone, hesitation, and context. A transcript may be word-perfect and still miss that the customer was unsure, buying time, or quietly objecting. For a small business owner, that matters when call notes from sales, support, or onboarding are used to decide the next step.

The bounded workflow decision is not whether AI should take over the work. It is whether you keep treating the transcript as the source of truth, or whether you add a check against the original audio or metadata before someone acts on it. That is a small control, not a replacement for human judgment.

A useful diagnostic question is: when we act on a transcript, how often do we later realise we missed hesitation or tone? Don’t guess. Pick 5–10 recent recordings, read the transcript, then listen to the audio beside it and mark every place where the transcript looked clear but the conversation was not.

If that review keeps surfacing the same ambiguity, the next step is to consider a small pilot that would test whether confidence scores, speaker intent, or similar markers would help the team read the conversation more honestly. Small truth, less drama.
